reflexion_entries_to_archive.lesson: Two separate docblocks in this repo asserted that the untargetable enumeration was complete — creatureAI.ts's 'THIS ONE LINE COVERS EVERY CREATURE-TARGETING PATH IN THE GAME' and untargetableGates.test.ts's 'THE BYPASSES WERE AUDITED RATHER THAN ASSUMED'. Both were written by sessions that had genuinely looked, and both were wrong: six paths of thirteen, and three files of fifteen. The carried handoff then repeated a SIX-item list whose most important member (world.ts's authoritative RAID_TARGET reducer) was never on it, and three of the six had wrong paths or line numbers. The fix is not a better audit; it is that the enumeration must be re-counted by a machine on every run. damage.wired.test.ts already had the pattern for exactly this reason and I reused it. ⭐ AND ITS ANTI-ROT ARM CAUGHT A STALE ENTRY ON ITS FIRST RUN — mine, a verdict about a file the census never reaches.

Every one of the six carried bypass sites was found by grepping for the CLAUSE, not by opening the recorded file:line. Three were wrong: src/controls.ts is src/input/controls.ts, voltkinChain is under creatures/ and the loop is at 106 not 92, seagullLifecycle is under seagulls/. Had I trusted the numbers I would have patched nothing and reported six fixes.

I planned an 'unkillable creature' — a guard at eight removal sites. The owner reframed it instead: 'he's in a different dimension, between realities... he's not really in the game.' That is not a softer version of my design, it is a cleaner one: a creature that has LEFT the world is not a candidate anywhere, where an unkillable one must be special-cased at every site that can acquire, strike or remove it. It also turned out to be the exact mechanism voltkin-config.ts:995 had predicted in writing for R121's submerged naga. ⇒ When the owner restates a mechanic in his own terms, read it as a design input, not as a looser spec.

Two of the new tests failed on their CONTROL arm first: a raid KILLS a chewer (so the landed raid is a removal, not a reduced pool) and resolveProjectileShot returns null unless the archer is ATTACKING inside the flight window. Both were fixture errors. A control that fails for the same reason the assertion would have is precisely how a vacuous test gets written and shipped green — so both diagnoses are recorded IN the tests rather than silently patched.

The A.0 probe returned 14/14, but the design panel lost 2 of 4 proposal lanes to the StructuredOutput retry cap (one on unescaped Windows backslashes in its JSON). Per the S161 rule those lanes are NOT DONE and are named as such in the PDR's PRIME-AUDIT delta; their angles were covered by hand. The panel that DID return found four things I had missed, including a ninth removal class (world.creatures.clear() at three sites) and the population latch that would have made a multi-cloud cone into N-1 silent no-ops.

Adding one CreatureType tripped four independent repo guards, and not one was a false alarm: the renderer-invisibility coverage test (the cloud drew nothing), the hand-maintained type list (the one site tsc cannot reach), the S169 'nothing is untargetable' assertion (correctly obsolete the moment the flag got its first consumer), and my OWN P2A acquisition census, which flagged bossSkillsPharaoh.ts on the very first file written after it shipped. ⭐ THE TEMPTING FIX WAS THE WRONG ONE TWICE: I could have satisfied the invisibility guard by dropping 'locustCloud' into GOBLIN_KINDS, which would have given a swarm of insects a HUMANOID puppet - satisfying the test while defeating its purpose; and I could have granted the Pharaoh a census verdict instead of recognising nearestEnemyFor as a genuinely guarded scanner. A guard is a question, not an obstacle: the right response is the answer, not the shortest thing that turns it green.

P2A's bindings pinned 'PROTOCOL_VERSION = 45 as const' as evidence for its no-bump claim. P2B bumped it to 46 - correctly - and the Stop hook hard-failed P2A as the S149 fabrication class. The claim was never 'the version is 45'; it was 'raRitualUntilTick is additive-optional and so costs no bump'. Rebound onto the MECHANISM that makes it true (the conditional emit/rehydrate pair in save.ts), which survives every future bump. verify-session-claims.py already warns about this exact class for json_field version keys - I walked into the file_contains version of the same trap.

Three separate carriers - boot-snapshot, session-state and the S170 PDR - had compressed R142's 'a cone of locusts THAT FLY AROUND IN LOCUST CLOUDS' to 'the locust cone', and the PDR hardened it further to 'wedge'. All describe a persistent cone VOLUME, which is a different mechanic from a fan of autonomous hunters. Reading the owner's verbatim words rather than the carried summary changed the template from the Kraken's sonar to the Warlord's direwolf summon. ⭐ AND MY OWN PDR CARRIED A VERSION OF THE SAME ERROR: it called the launch 'a reuse of inCone'. inCone is a MEMBERSHIP test; the launch PLACES. It became the test ORACLE instead, which is a real check where building the launch on it would have been circular.

The ritual's five columns are timed so the last one lands on the exact tick the channel ends. My runner checked death first, removed the boss, and silently dropped that column - the ultimate would have shipped as four columns and a corpse, and it would have LOOKED fine. What caught it was that the test counts columns by standing a real victim on each landing spot and asserting all five die. A spy on applyRadialDamage, a call-count, or a vaguer 'columns landed' assertion would every one of them have been green on four of five. ⇒ When a mechanic's value is N of something, assert N OUTCOMES, not N invocations.

The atlas guard reported 30 sheets clean while the owner could see two of them were dirty. The instinct is to loosen a threshold; the truth was that neither defect was a threshold problem. It measured HEIGHT on a creature whose scale lives in WIDTH (scarab: width dev 0.27, height 0.01), and it measured the bbox of ALL opaque pixels so one stray sliver redefined the animal (188px against a 136px beetle). Both were found by dumping the metric across all 48 atlases and looking at the distribution, and the two sheets he named came out ranks 1 and 2. ⇒ When a guard disagrees with the owner's eyes, print its raw numbers for the whole population before touching a constant - the ranking tells you whether the metric or the threshold is wrong.

My first instinct for the white fringe was 'threshold on TOTAL instead of largest blob'. The existing docblock had explicitly considered and rejected exactly that, with data: eye glints give healthy sheets 66-768px of total white while their largest pocket is 2-52px, so summing calls the healthy sheets worse than the broken ones. It was right. Reading it turned a wrong fix into the correct one - the discriminator is not how much white but WHERE: a glint is interior, a matte fringe hugs the cut-out edge. ⇒ A comment that pre-refutes your change is the cheapest review you will ever get; the fix that survives it is a better fix.

Twice in one session vitest went fully green while `tsc -b` inside `npm run build` failed on a type error in a TEST file - once a missing property on a return type, once an unused binding. vitest strips types, so a test suite passing says nothing about the test file compiling, and the failure surfaces two gates later where it reads as a build break rather than as the test edit that caused it.

s170_priorities_archived.check_method: FOG OF WAR, FOURTH AND CORRECT ATTEMPT - per-entity CULLING, the C&C model. Owner: "look at Red Alert. Theyre, like, from the fucking nineties. They did it fine." The classic model is 3 parts and this repo already had 2: the explored grid (exploredMemory -> dark/dim/clear tiers) and remembered last-seen buildings (S60 ghosts). The missing third - units in non-visible cells are simply NOT DRAWN - was the entire complaint. render/concealment.ts computes vision ONCE per frame (beginConcealmentFrame; the sources walk is O(own prims + creatures) so per-entity would be quadratic) and isConcealed(x,y,owner) is a cheap read, wired into all 10 renderers that draw his hide-list. Own entities never concealed (owner check before geometry). Bond hidden unless BOTH ends visible. structureRenderer skips BEFORE seen.add so leaving vision REAPS the sprite. Gatherer cull is in the unit loop only, because that renderer also draws the CASTLE (his one always-visible exception). "until they are in the center which is lit" needed no special case - the spawner disc is already a permanent vision source for every seat. ALSO IN P1: groundLayer at stage bottom so the 0.55-alpha backdrop stops compositing over sparks/bonds/primitives (the S166 report, live through two prior "fixes"); border walls restored to visible (R162); own-zone full-rect erase so your quadrant is lit corner to corner, not just around structures. THREE MECHANISMS WERE TRIED AND REMOVED: backdrop above the sheet (S166 class), below it (S169 class), and an inverse Pixi mask - the last shipped twice concealing nothing, first because the mask texture was tinted FOG_COLOR (a Pixi alpha mask samples a colour CHANNEL and the red channel of black is 0 everywhere), then because the mechanism was UNTESTABLE (Pixi implements alpha masks as filters; renderer.extract does not apply filter effects, so no assertion in the repo could see whether the board was concealed). Untestability was the real defect. Culling is a pure predicate: 12 tests incl. "the fog closes behind you when the spark leaves" (which forbids sticky concealment - remembering WHERE buildings were is the ghost layer, not this predicate) and "nothing concealed during FIGHT" (R62).
